Rashi on Chullin 5b:1:1.hebrew: מעם - ולא כל עם, וגבי חטאת כתיב שבא ע"י השוגג:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:1:1.english: Me'am [some of the people] - and not all the people; and regarding a sin-offering it is written that it comes on account of an unwitting [sin].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:10:1.english: And then he resolved [it] - [it was] Rabbi Zeira, for himself.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:10:2.hebrew: מסתברא שמיע להו ולא קבלוה, דאי ס"ד לא שמיע להו, ואי שמיע להו הוו מקבלי לה:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:10:2.english: It stands to reason that they had heard it and did not accept it, for if it should enter your mind that they had not heard it — but had they heard it, they would have accepted it.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:10:3.hebrew: היכי מסתייע מילתא למיכל כו' - היאך יגרום שום שטן לפני צדיקים, ע"י שוגג, שום דבר עון:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:10:3.english: How did the matter eventuate, leading them to eat, etc. - How could any adversary (mishap) cause, before the righteous, through inadvertence, any matter of sin?

Rashi on Chullin 5b:10:4.english: Now, [through] the animals of the righteous - [This refers to] the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, [related] further on.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:10:5.english: The Holy One, blessed be He, does not bring a stumbling block through them - [meaning] that the animal would eat something forbidden to it.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:2:1.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei says - From here you learn [this].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:2:2.hebrew: אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה ואשם - וסמיך ליה או הודע אליו חטאתו אשר חטא והביא אשמו, דמשמע אשר לא תעשינה, אם היה יודע שהוא אסור ושגגה היתה לו וחטא ואשם - הוא יביא:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:2:2.english: Which may not be done, unwittingly, and he becomes guilty - And juxtaposed to it [in the next verse] is, "or if his sin, which he committed, becomes known to him, he shall bring his guilt-offering," which implies that "which may not be done" [refers to a case where] he knew that it was forbidden, and it was an unwitting error for him, and he sinned and is guilty - he shall bring [an offering].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:2:3.hebrew: השב מידיעתו - שאם היה יודע שהוא חלב, היה יושב ומבטל מעבירה זו. ואית דגריס השב, והוא נמי הפורש ונבדל מתחלה, ואין עובר אם היה יודע שהוא אסור. ובת"כ גרס היושב:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:2:3.english: One who refrains due to his knowledge - [Meaning] that if he had known that it was forbidden fat, he would have sat and abstained from this transgression. And there are those who read [the text simply as] "one who refrains" (השב) [without "מידיעתו"], and this too [refers to] one who withdraws and separates from the outset, and does not transgress, if he had known that it was forbidden. And in Torat Kohanim the reading is "one who sits" (היושב).

Rashi on Chullin 5b:3:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - מ"מ מומר לא מקבלינן מיניה, בין למר בין למר, ואפילו שוגג, דהא אילו היה יודע מתחלה נמי היה אוכלו, ואין שב מידיעתו:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:3:1.english: What is [the difference] between them? - In any case, we do not accept [meat slaughtered by] an apostate, whether according to this opinion or that opinion, even [if it was done] unwittingly, for even if he had known [the law] from the start he would have eaten it anyway, and he would not repent through his [now] knowing [it].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:3:2.hebrew: והביא קרבן על הדם - ששגג בו, ואילו היה יודע שהוא דם לא היה אוכלו. לת"ק, מומר שמו ולא מקבלינן מיניה. ולר"ש, שב מידיעתו הוא בדם, ומקבלינן מיניה:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:3:2.english: And he brought an offering for the blood - He erred in this unwittingly, and had he known that it was blood he would not have eaten it. According to the first tanna, he is termed an apostate (mumar), and we do not accept [an offering] from him. But according to Rabbi Shimon, with regard to the blood he is one who would repent once aware [of his sin], and so we do accept [an offering] from him.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:1.hebrew: מכם ולא כולכם - דלעיל בעולת נדבה משתעי קרא, דכתיב בתריה: אם עולה קרבנו וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:1.english: "From you" and not "all of you" - [This is derived from the verse] above [Leviticus 1:2], which speaks of a voluntary burnt-offering, as it is written afterward: "If his offering is a burnt-offering, etc." [Leviticus 1:3].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:2.hebrew: דלכפרה הוא - וכיון דדעתו להזיד ולחזור על עבירתו, ובהא מיהא אתרמי דשגג ולא הזיד, א"כ אמאי נקבל מיניה, הא לאו בר כפרה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:2.english: That it is for atonement - Since his intent [in general] is to sin deliberately and return to his transgression, and in this instance it merely happened that he sinned unwittingly and not deliberately - if so, why should we accept [the offering] from him? He is not one who is fit for atonement.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:3.hebrew: דלאו חיובא - ולאו אורח ארעא לקבולי דורון מיניה, דכתיב זבח רשעים תועבה (משלי כא):
Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:3.english: That it is not an obligation - and it is likewise not proper conduct to accept a gift from him, as it is written: "The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination" (Proverbs 21).

Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:4.english: But a sin-offering that is an obligation - it is a debt that rests upon him.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:4:5.english: Say, let us accept [it] from him - So that a sinner should not profit [from his transgression, by being absolved of an obligation that others must fulfill].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:5:1.english: It is a deficiency - for you established above that [Scripture] calls transgressors "an animal."

Rashi on Chullin 5b:5:2.hebrew: שהן ערומים בדעת - כאדם הראשון, ומשימין עצמן כבהמה דכאי רוח:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:5:2.english: That they are shrewd in knowledge - Like Adam, the first man, and [yet] they make themselves like cattle, humble/lowly in spirit.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:6:1.hebrew: וזרע בהמה - ומוקמינן לה במסכת סוטה (דף כב.): לא קרא ולא שנה ולא שמש תלמידי חכמים, עליו הכתוב אומר: וזרעתי את בית ישראל זרע אדם וזרע בהמה, כלומר החכמים והבורים, כולם אזרעם לפרותם ולרבותם:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:6:1.english: And seed of animal - And we interpret this in tractate Sotah (22a): [Regarding] one who did not read Scripture, nor learn Mishnah, nor serve Torah scholars, about him Scripture says: "And I will sow the house of Israel with seed of man and seed of animal" [Jeremiah 31:27] - meaning, the wise and the boors, I will sow all of them, to make them fruitful and increase them.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:8:1.hebrew: ר"ג - בנו של ר' יהודה הנשיא, שהיה מן האחרונים, ובית דינו נמנו על שחיטת כותי, לאחר שנשנית משנתינו דהכל שוחטין ואפילו כותי, ואסרוה:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:8:1.english: R. Gamliel - the son of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who was of the later generation [of Sages]; and his court took a vote regarding the slaughtering [performed] by a Samaritan, after our Mishnah - which teaches that "all may slaughter, even a Samaritan" - had already been taught, and they prohibited it.

Rashi on Chullin 5b:8:2.english: Rabbi did not hear, etc. - This, too, is like our Mishnah [teaches].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:8:3.english: "Does it need to be said?" - But is it not obvious to us that they [Samaritans] are not bound by [the prohibition of] "you shall not place a stumbling block before the blind" (Leviticus 19)?

Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:1.hebrew: קבלה מיניה - רבי זירא מר' יעקב, דאפילו כשישראל עומד על גביו אסור, או לא קבלה:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:1.english: Did he accept it from him - [that is, did] Rabbi Zeira [accept] from Rabbi Yaakov [bar Idi the ruling] that even when a Jew is standing over him [supervising the Samaritan's slaughter] it is forbidden, or did he not accept [it].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:2.hebrew: אכל משחיטת כותי - בישראל עומד על גביו, או ע"י שחתך כזית בשר ונתן לו ואכל, ואף ר' אסי אכל:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:2.english: He ate from the slaughter of a Samaritan (Kuthite) - [This was] where a Jew stood over him [supervising the slaughter], or where [the Samaritan] cut off an olive-sized piece of meat and gave it to him, and he ate it - and even Rabbi Asi ate [in this manner].

Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:3.hebrew: ותהי בה רבי זירא גרסינן מתמיה - עליהן שאכלוה, ומבעיא ליה בלביה הכי:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:3.english: "And Rabbi Zeira wondered about it" (ותהי בה) - we read this as an expression of astonishment - about them, [Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Asi,] that they had eaten it, and this is what he was puzzling over in his heart:

Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:4.hebrew: לא שמיע להו - הא דנמנו ר"ג, דאי שמיע להו הוו מקבלי, או דלמא שמיע ולא קבלוה:
Rashi on Chullin 5b:9:4.english: They had not heard it - This refers to that which Rabban Gamliel and his court voted [to prohibit]: that if they had heard it, they would have accepted it, or perhaps they heard it and did not accept it.

Tosafot on Chullin 5b:10:1.hebrew: צדיקים עצמן לא כ"ש - תימה, דהא אשכחן יהודה בן טבאי שהרג עד זומם, בפ"ק דמכות (דף ה:), ור' ישמעאל שקרא והטה, בפ"ק דשבת (דף יב:). ואור"י דדוקא במידי דאכילה אין הקב"ה מביא תקלה על ידן, שגנאי הוא לצדיק שאוכל דבר איסור. ולספרים דגרסי (בפ"ק) דכתובות (דף כח:) גבי העלה עבד לכהונה על פיו: "השתא בהמתן של צדיקים" כו', משום דאתי לידי אכילת איסור, שמאכיל בת ישראל שנשאת לו בתרומה, והוא עבד ואין לו בה קדושין. ומיהו ברוב ספרים לא גרסינן ליה, והיינו משום דליכא למפרך אלא כשהצדיק עצמו אוכל האיסור. ובר"ה (דף כא.) דאמר "כמה בסים תבשילא דבבלאי" בצומא רבא דמערבא, ובערבי פסחים (דף קו:) ר' ירמיה בר אבא איקלע לבי רב אסי ואשתלי וטעם קודם הבדלה, אע"ג דמיתתו באסכרה - התם אכילת היתר הוא, אלא שאוכל בשעה האסורה. ובבראשית רבה גרס: ר' ירמיה דשדר לר' זירא כלכלה דפירי בין דין לדין, אתאכיל פירי בטבלייהו. ומיהו ההוא עובדא איתא במסכתא שקלים (דף ח.), וקאמר עלה ר' זירא: אם הראשונים כמלאכים אנו כבר אינש, ואם הראשונים כבני אינש אנו כחמורים, ולא כחמורו דר' פנחס בן יאיר: [ע"ע תוס' שבת דף יב: ד"ה רבי נתן, ותוספות פסחים קו: ד"ה אישתלי, ותוספות יבמות צט: ד"ה ס"ד, ותוספות גיטין ז. ד"ה השתא]:
Tosafot on Chullin 5b:10:1.english: The righteous themselves, all the more so - This is astonishing, for we find that Yehuda ben Tabai killed a false witness (eid zomem) [in error], in the first chapter of Makkot (5b), and that Rabbi Yishmael read [by a lamp] and tilted it [on Shabbat], in the first chapter of Shabbat (12b) - both righteous men who stumbled. And the Ri explains that specifically with regard to matters of eating does the Holy One not bring about stumbling through them, because it is a disgrace for a righteous person to eat something forbidden [but He does not shield them from other kinds of error]. And according to the texts that have the reading, in the first chapter of Ketubot (28b), regarding [the case of] one who raised a slave to the priesthood on his own word: "Now, the animals of the righteous..." etc. - [the same is said there] because it leads to eating something forbidden, in that he causes a Jewish woman who married him to eat teruma, while he is [in fact] a slave and has no valid kiddushin (marriage) with her [so she eats teruma without entitlement]. However, most texts do not have this reading, and that is because the difficulty can only be raised when the righteous person himself eats the forbidden item [not when he merely causes someone else to do so]. And [what of] Rosh Hashanah (21a), where it is said, "How tasty is the dish of the Babylonians!" - said on the great fast day according to the reckoning of the West (Eretz Yisrael) [without realizing it was Yom Kippur] - and [what of] "Arvei Pesachim" (106b), [where] Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba happened to be at the house of Rav Assi, forgot, and tasted [food] before Havdalah, even though his death was by askara (a throat ailment, taken as a sign of sin)? There, it is the eating of a permitted item, only that he eats it at a forbidden time - [which is a different matter from eating forbidden food itself]. And in Bereishit Rabbah the text reads: Rabbi Yirmeya sent Rabbi Zeira a basket of fruit between one session and the next, and the fruit was eaten while still tevel (untithed produce). However, that incident is also found in Tractate Shekalim (8a), where Rabbi Zeira says about it: "If the earlier generations were like angels, we are like [ordinary] men; and if the earlier generations were like men, we are like donkeys - and not even like the donkey of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair [which famously would not eat untithed produce]." [See also Tosafot on Shabbat 12b s.v. "Rabbi Natan"; Tosafot on Pesachim 106b s.v. "ishtali"; Tosafot on Yevamot 99b s.v. "salka da'atach"; and Tosafot on Gittin 7a s.v. "hashta."]

Tosafot on Chullin 5b:1:1.hebrew: מעם הארץ פרט למומר - תימה, דמאי קאמר: הא מהכא נפקא, מהתם נפקא? הא אדרבה הך פליגא, דאפילו מומר לדבר אחד קאמר ת"ק דאין מקבלין, דהא מוקמינן דפליגי באוכל חלב והפריש קרבן על הדם, ודוחק לומר דפריך מדר"ש. ומפרש ר"ת דמומר לאכול חלב היינו מומר לכל התורה חוץ מדם, כדאשכחן שכולל כל החטאות בכלל חטאת חלב בפ"ק דמנחות (דף ו.) ובפרק היה מביא (סוטה דף טו.) דאמר בדין שתהא חטאת חלב טעונה נסכים. והשתא קאמר דלת"ק כשהוא מומר לכל התורה כולה חוץ מדם אינו מביא קרבן על הדם, ולר"ש מביא, כיון שהוא שב מידיעתו מדם, אבל מומר לדבר אחד דברי הכל מביא. ועוי"ל דדוקא בחלב ודם פליגי, לפי שהם שוין שיש כרת בשניהן ועולין לגבוה, ונאמרו בלאו אחד "כל חלב וכל דם לא תאכלו", דלת"ק חשיב ליה מומר לאותו דבר כאילו הוא מומר לדם עצמו, ואינו מניח בשביל האיסור אלא משום דנפשו קצה לאכול דם, אבל מומר לאחד משאר איסורים פשיטא דמביא קרבן על הדם, ולר"ש אפילו מומר לאכול חלב מביא קרבן על הדם:
Tosafot on Chullin 5b:1:1.english: From the people of the land - excluding an apostate - It is difficult: what is [the Gemara] saying? Does this [law] derive from here, or does it derive from there? On the contrary, this [matter] is itself disputed, for the first tanna (Tana Kamma) says that even regarding an apostate with respect to one matter (mumar l'davar echad), one does not accept [an offering] from him, since we establish that they [Tana Kamma and R' Shimon] disagree about a case of one who eats cheilev (forbidden fat) and sets aside an offering for [inadvertently eating] blood. And it is a forced reading to say that [the Gemara] is asking [only] from the words of R' Shimon. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that "an apostate to eat cheilev" means an apostate with regard to the entire Torah except for blood, as we find that [the Torah] includes all sin-offerings within the category of the sin-offering for cheilev, in the first chapter of Menachot (6a) and in the chapter "Hayah Meivi" (Sotah 15a), where it says that by right the sin-offering for cheilev should require libations (nesachim) [like the others that require them]. And now [Tosafot] explains that according to Tana Kamma, when he is an apostate with regard to the entire Torah except for blood, he does not bring an offering for [inadvertently eating] blood, but according to R' Shimon he does bring [an offering], since he deliberately refrains from blood [alone, out of genuine conviction]; but an apostate regarding [only] one matter, all agree he brings [an offering]. And furthermore, one can say that specifically regarding cheilev and blood do they disagree, because they are alike in that there is karet [for eating] both, and both are offered up [on the altar], and they are stated in one prohibition: "all cheilev and all blood you shall not eat" - so that according to Tana Kamma, he considers him an apostate regarding that matter [cheilev] as if he were an apostate regarding blood itself, and he refrains [from blood] not because of the prohibition but only because his soul is disgusted by eating blood; but an apostate regarding one of the other prohibitions, obviously he brings an offering for blood. And according to R' Shimon, even an apostate to eat cheilev brings an offering for blood.

Tosafot on Chullin 5b:2:1.hebrew: אינו שב מידיעתו אינו מביא קרבן על שגגתו - תימה, מה צריך קרא למעט לאינו שב מידיעתו ועומד ברשעו, הא הוי זבח רשעים, והיכי תיסק אדעתין לומר דמביא? ויש לומר, דאיצטריך להיכא דחזר בתשובה אח"כ, ובשעה שאכל לא היה שב מידיעתו:
Tosafot on Chullin 5b:2:1.english: One who does not repent because of his own knowledge does not bring an offering for his unwitting sin - It is difficult: why does the verse need to exclude one who does not repent because of his own knowledge and remains in his wickedness - this is [in any case] "the sacrifice of the wicked" [which is not accepted], so how could it occur to us to say that he brings [an offering]? And one could say: it is necessary for a case where he repented afterward, but at the time that he ate [i.e., sinned unwittingly], he was not [yet] one who repents because of his own knowledge.

Tosafot on Chullin 5b:8:1.hebrew: ר"ג ובית דינו נמנו על שחיטת כותי ואסרוה - פירש בקונטרס: ר"ג בנו של ר' יהודה הנשיא, שהיה אחרון. וכן משמע קצת, דקאמר בסמוך ר"ג ובית דינו כר"מ ס"ל דחייש למיעוטא, משמע שהוא ר"ג אחרון שהיה אחר ר"מ. ומיהו קשה, דא"כ הויא ליה לפרושי בהדיא ר"ג בנו של ר"י הנשיא, כדתנן במס' אבות (פ"ב מ"ב): ר"ג בנו של ר' יהודה הנשיא אומר יפה תלמוד תורה עם דרך ארץ. ועוד תימה, דגזר ר"מ על סתם יינם, ולא גזר על שחיטה דאורייתא. אבל אם הוא ר"ג דיבנה ניחא, והא דקאמר כר"מ סבירא להו משום דר"מ ס"ל הכי בהדיא. אבל קשה, דא"כ סבר ר"ג דיבנה דכותים גרי אמת הן, כיון דשחיטתן הויא שריא קודם גזירה. ובריש הדר (עירובין סא.) תנן: הדר עם העובד כוכבים או עם מי שאינו מודה בעירוב, ה"ז אסור. פירוש אינו מודה בעירוב היינו כותי, כדאמר בפרק בכל מערבין (עירובין לא:): ר"א ב"ר יעקב אומר עד שיהיו שני ישראלים אוסרים זה על זה, ר"ג אומר צדוקי אינו כעובד כוכבים, ופירש בקונטרס אבל כותי הוי כעובד כוכבים, דקסבר כותים גרי אריות הן. מיהו ע"כ א"א לומר כפירוש הקונטרס, דהא ר"ג דיבנה אית ליה בהדיא בפ"ק דגיטין (דף י.) דגרי אמת הן, שהכשיר גט שעדיו עדי כותים. והיינו יכולין לפרש אבל כותי הוי כעובד כוכבים משום דאינו מודה בעירוב, דהיינו נמי טעמא דת"ק דאסר, שהוא ר"מ, כדמוכח התם בגמרא, ור"מ אית ליה התם (בבכורות) דכותים גרי אמת הן. אבל קשה, כיון דלכ"ע כותי אוסר אע"ג דגרי אמת הן, א"כ מה באו לחדש ר' אמי ור' אסי שעשאום עובדי כוכבים גמורין לבטל רשות וליתן רשות, הא מעיקרא נמי הכי הוה לכ"ע. אלא י"ל דלר"ג כותי נמי אינו כעובד כוכבים, ותנן צדוקי אינו כעובד כוכבים, וה"ה לכותים דגרי אמת הן, והיו סבורין דגרי אמת הן כר"ג, עד שעשאום רבי אמי ור' אסי עובדי כוכבים גמורין. אע"ג דרבי יוחנן פסק כר' אליעזר בר' יעקב, ור' אליעזר בר' יעקב לא פליג את"ק שאוסר כותי, ר' יוחנן לא בא לפסוק כמותו אלא במה שצריך שיהו שני ישראלים אוסרים זה על זה:
Tosafot on Chullin 5b:8:1.english: Rabban Gamliel and his court took a vote regarding the slaughter of a Samaritan (Kuti) and prohibited it - Rashi explains: this is Rabban Gamliel the son of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who was the latter [Rabban Gamliel], and this is also somewhat implied by the fact that it says shortly afterward, "Rabban Gamliel and his court hold like Rabbi Meir, who is concerned for the minority [view]" - implying that he is the latter Rabban Gamliel, who lived after Rabbi Meir. However, this is difficult, for if so, it should have stated explicitly "Rabban Gamliel the son of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi," as we learn in Tractate Avot (2:2): "Rabban Gamliel the son of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: Torah study is good together with an occupation (derech eretz)." And it is further difficult: [if so,] Rabbi Meir decreed regarding their ordinary wine (setam yeinam) [that it is forbidden, a merely rabbinic matter], yet did not decree regarding [their] slaughter, which would be a Torah-level [prohibition, and thus the more serious concern]? But if it is Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, this fits well - and the statement that "they hold like Rabbi Meir" is because Rabbi Meir explicitly holds this view [elsewhere]. But this is [still] difficult: if so, Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh holds that Samaritans are true converts (geirei emet), since their slaughter was permitted before the decree. Yet at the beginning of [the chapter] "HaDar" (Eruvin 61a) we learn: "One who dwells [in a courtyard] with a gentile, or with someone who does not acknowledge the eruv, this [renders the courtyard] forbidden." The explanation of "does not acknowledge the eruv" is a Samaritan, as it says in the chapter "BaKol Me'arvin" (Eruvin 31b): Rabbi Eliezer bar Yaakov says [the courtyard is forbidden only] once there are two Jews prohibiting it to one another; Rabban Gamliel says a Sadducee is not like a gentile - and Rashi explains: but a Samaritan is like a gentile, for he [Rabban Gamliel] holds that Samaritans are "converts of lions" (geirei arayot, i.e., insincere converts who converted out of fear). However, it must be that one cannot say this in accordance with Rashi's explanation, for Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh explicitly holds, in the first chapter of Gittin (10a), that they are true converts - since he validated a divorce document (get) whose witnesses were Samaritans. Instead, we can explain [his statement] this way: a Samaritan is [treated] like a gentile because he does not acknowledge the eruv - which is also the reason of the first Tanna (tana kama) who prohibits [in the eruv mishnah], who is Rabbi Meir, as is proven there in the Gemara; and Rabbi Meir holds there (in Bechorot) that Samaritans are true converts. But this is [still] difficult: since according to everyone a Samaritan renders [the courtyard] forbidden even though he is a true convert, then what novelty did Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Assi introduce when they made them into complete gentiles for [the purposes of] revoking [a share in the courtyard, i.e., through sale] and granting a share - was this not the same from the outset according to everyone? Rather, one must say that according to Rabban Gamliel a Samaritan, too, is not like a gentile - for we learned "a Sadducee is not like a gentile," and the same applies to Samaritans, since they are true converts - and [the authorities] used to think that they were true converts, following Rabban Gamliel's view, until Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Assi made them complete gentiles. [This remains true] even though Rabbi Yochanan ruled in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer bar Yaakov, for Rabbi Eliezer bar Yaakov does not disagree with the first Tanna who prohibits [in the case of] a Samaritan - Rabbi Yochanan came to rule like him only regarding the requirement that there be two Jews prohibiting one another.
